passages.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.
passages.sermon:
People have reported something about you.
They say there is sexual immorality among you.
This kind of immorality is very serious.
Even people who do not know God do not accept this.
A man among you has his father’s wife.
passages.original: Ὅλως ἀκούεται ἐν ὑμῖν πορνεία καὶ τοιαύτη πορνεία ἥτις οὐδὲ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὥστε γυναῖκά τινα τοῦ πατρὸς ἔχειν

passages.text: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?
passages.sermon:
You are proud.
You should not be proud.
You should feel deep sorrow.
You should remove the man who did this from your group.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς πεφυσιωμένοι ἐστέ καὶ οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἐπενθήσατε ἵνα ἀρθῇ ἐκ μέσου ὑμῶν ὁ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο πράξας

passages.text: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.
passages.sermon:
Paul is not with the Corinthians in person.
Paul is away from them in body.
Paul is with them in spirit.
Paul has already judged the man who committed this sin.
Paul judged him as if he were present with them.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν γάρ ἀπὼν τῷ σώματι παρὼν δὲ τῷ πνεύματι ἤδη κέκρικα ὡς παρὼν τὸν οὕτως τοῦτο κατεργασάμενον

passages.text: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus, hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul is not physically present with the church.
Paul is present with the church in spirit.
The church gathers together in the name of the Lord Jesus.
The power of the Lord Jesus is with them.
Paul instructs the church to act together.
Paul tells them to hand over the man who sinned.
They must give this man to Satan.
This will destroy his flesh.
This will save his spirit on the Day of the Lord.
passages.original: ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ συναχθέντων ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πνεύματος σὺν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ παραδοῦναι τὸν τοιοῦτον τῷ Σατανᾷ εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκός ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα σωθῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul rebuked the church for their pride.
Your boasting is not good.
A little leaven affects the whole batch of dough.
Even a small amount of sin can influence the entire community.
passages.original: Οὐ καλὸν τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ

passages.text: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the church in Corinth.
Paul told the believers to remove the old leaven.
Leaven means sin or corrupting influence.
Paul wanted them to become a new batch of dough.
This new batch should be without leaven.
Paul said they already are unleavened.
Christ is our Passover lamb.
Christ has been sacrificed for us.
passages.original: ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι καὶ γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός

passages.text: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the church in Corinth.
Paul told them to celebrate the feast.
We must not use the old bread.
The old bread has leaven.
Leaven stands for malice and wickedness.
We must use new bread without leaven.
This new bread stands for sincerity and truth.
passages.original: ὥστε ἑορτάζωμεν μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας καὶ πονηρίας ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας

passages.text: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul wrote a letter to the church.
Paul told the church not to associate with sexually immoral people.
passages.original: Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι πόρνοις

passages.text: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote a letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul told them not to associate with certain people.
Paul did not mean the sexually immoral people of this world.
Paul did not mean the greedy people of this world.
Paul did not mean the swindlers of this world.
Paul did not mean the idolaters of this world.
If Paul meant those people, the church would have to leave this world.
passages.original: οὐ πάντως τοῖς πόρνοις τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἢ τοῖς πλεονέκταις καὶ ἅρπαξιν ἢ εἰδωλολάτραις ἐπεὶ ὠφείλετε ἄρα ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελθεῖν

passages.text: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul gives instructions to believers.
Paul says, “Do not associate with anyone who claims to be a brother.”
A brother is someone who calls himself a Christian.
Do not associate if this person is sexually immoral.
Do not associate if this person is greedy.
Do not associate if this person is an idolater.
Do not associate if this person is a verbal abuser.
Do not associate if this person is a drunkard.
Do not associate if this person is a swindler.
Do not even eat with such a person.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι ἐάν τις ἀδελφὸς ὀνομαζόμενος ᾖ πόρνος ἢ πλεονέκτης ἢ εἰδωλολάτρης ἢ λοίδορος ἢ μέθυσος ἢ ἅρπαξ τῷ τοιούτῳ μηδὲ συνεσθίειν

passages.text: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul speaks to the church.
\r\nPaul asks a question.
\r\nPaul says, "It is not my business to judge people outside the church."
\r\nPaul says, "You are responsible to judge those inside the church."
passages.original: Τί γάρ μοι τοὺς ἔξω κρίνειν οὐχὶ τοὺς ἔσω ὑμεῖς κρίνετε

passages.text: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”
passages.sermon: God judges people who are outside the church.\r\nYou must remove the wicked person from among yourselves.
passages.original: τοὺς δὲ ἔξω ὁ Θεὸς κρίνει Ἐξάρατε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν
